title: Home fire
aliases: there is a fire in my kitchen
tldr: Get out, stay out and call emergency services from outside. Use the nearest safe exit, stay low beneath smoke, and close doors behind you if possible. Do not stop for belongings or go back inside for people or pets; tell firefighters where they may be.
steps: Follow the escape route and use stairs, not elevators. Check doors for heat before opening; use another exit if unsafe.
Close doors between you and fire, call emergency services with your location and signal from a window.
Account for everyone at the meeting point and report missing people to firefighters.
Do not reenter until the fire department permits it.
next: Install and test smoke alarms and practice two ways out with the household. Plan assistance for children and people with mobility needs.
watch: An extinguisher attempt must never delay escape or block your exit.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Escape immediately, gather outside and keep the exit area clear. If trapped, close the door between you and smoke, signal from a window and send your exact location if possible. Do not reenter because the fire seems quiet or because firefighters have not arrived.
household: Practice the route with children and anyone needing movement assistance. Agree on a nearby meeting point and who will supervise dependents once outside. Include a second safe way out when the building permits it; never block an exit with stored supplies.
pack_now: Prioritize supplies named in this guide that are usable by the person who needs them. Keep the checklist and relevant contact details accessible. Check carrying capacity, storage and equipment instructions in advance; collecting equipment must not delay the immediate protective action.

When the first option is unavailable

Escape immediately, gather outside and keep the exit area clear. If trapped, close the door between you and smoke, signal from a window and send your exact location if possible. Do not reenter because the fire seems quiet or because firefighters have not arrived.
faqs: Can I retrieve a phone or a pet?

Do not delay escape or reenter for belongings or animals. Once outside, tell responders where anyone may remain. Keep the household assembly point clear so missing people can be identified without people searching inside.
The exit is blocked — what then?

Do not force a hot door or a route filling with smoke. Close doors between you and the fire, call and signal your exact location. A high-rise needs its building-specific plan; use the Apartment & high-rise fire guide rather than guessing at an elevator or window escape.
scope: Civilian educational guidance. Linked references may use U.S. emergency systems; local warning methods, laws, services and conditions differ.
